purpose: Hand-authored claims of which theories/<Module>.v are checked, by a differential test, against the ACTUAL shipped production OCaml — not merely against the extracted Rocq model in isolation. This is a distinct question from 'is it proven': every theorem in proof-ledger.json is proven either way. It is the backlog-201 answer to 'model vs production' for this project, made mechanical rather than left to README/STATUS prose. scripts/check-production-link.py verifies each entry below against the freshly generated ledger (the module must exist in it — its theorem count is read from the ledger, not separately declared or cross-checked here) and the named test file's real content (production_call must appear as a live reference, comments and string literals stripped — a stale claim whose test regressed must fail, not silently keep being cited).
no_anti_drift_check: Disclosed gap (backlog-201 round-1 architect finding, not fixed by this change): unlike formal/codegen-ptx/production-link.json's PtxLayout entry, NEITHER module below has an extraction-vs-committed byte-compare. formal/type-safety/_CoqProject lists only theories/*.v — extraction/TypeSafetyExtraction.v and extraction/UnifyExtraction.v do not exist, so the committed TypeSafetyModel.ml / UnifyModel.ml the differential tests below run against are never regenerated or drift-checked by scripts/check-formal-proofs.sh (its byte-compare at line ~282 is guarded by `basename == codegen-ptx` and does not run for this project at all). Practical consequence: TypeSafetySpec.v or UnifySpec.v can be edited, re-proven, and re-counted, and this gate and check-formal-proofs.sh will both stay green, while TypeSafetyModel.ml / UnifyModel.ml — and therefore what T1-CMBT/T2-UNIFY actually test against — silently keep testing the OLDER extraction. This is a real gap in what 'checked against production' means for this project's 44 theorems, not merely a documentation omission; closing it (adding the two extraction drivers and generalising the drift check beyond the codegen-ptx basename guard) is out of scope for backlog-201 and is tracked as follow-up work, not implemented here.

TypeSafetySpec.note: T1-CMBT differential property (QCheck, 2000 RANDOMLY SAMPLED cases, not exhaustive): asserts the extracted TypeSafetyModel.infer_type and the real Sarek_typer.infer agree, over the ELit/EVar/ELet/ETuple fragment the model covers. F-TS-01 (ELet scope leak) was found this way and is resolved. Sampling establishes agreement on the inputs generated, not universally — a counterexample outside the sampled space is exactly what this evidence cannot rule out.

UnifySpec.note: T2-UNIFY differential property (QCheck, 1000 RANDOMLY SAMPLED cases, not exhaustive): asserts the extracted unifier and the real Sarek_types.unify agree, over ground (non-type-variable) types. Same sampling caveat as TypeSafetySpec above.
